jasmin: Noticed a nasty one in the Python sampleapp: request-id sometimes disappears from logs (or shows an old value) after async awaits, even though OTEL spans have the correct id. This only triggers with REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug and under small concurrency. Could be contextvar propagation + redaction interplay.

jasmin: Quick repro I used locally:
```bash
git clone git@github.com:redwood/sampleapp.git
cd examples/python_fastapi
python -m venv venv; source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug uvicorn server:app --reload
# run a small script that fires many concurrent requests with a client that retries once
python tests/concurrent_retries.py
```
Observed: some log lines show request-id: "[REDACTED]" or an earlier request id, while the OTEL span attribute `request.id` has the correct latest id. It looks like: logging filter picks up a contextvar value that was set before an awaited call that mutated headers; later the retry wrapper updates header and span attribs but the contextvar used by the Python logging filter wasn't updated in that coroutine.

tom: interesting. might be our use of contextvars + some middleware doing `scope['headers'][...] = ...` which doesn't update the contextvar used by logger. Do you have exact snippets?

jasmin: log excerpt:
```
[2026-05-22T15:02:01.101Z] INFO  uvicorn.access  <-- POST /chat { request-id: "rid-py-001" }
[2026-05-22T15:02:01.105Z] DEBUG retry         retrying, set header x-request-id: "rid-py-002"
[2026-05-22T15:02:01.110Z] DEBUG otel          span.start attrs: request.id=rid-py-002
[2026-05-22T15:02:01.112Z] DEBUG logger        log emitted, request-id: rid-py-001
```
Packages: redwood-telemetry-py==0.6.4, redwood-sdk==1.4.3, opentelemetry-api==1.14.0, Python 3.11.

rekha: i've debugged similar before: Python logging integration reads from a contextvar that we set during initial middleware. If a later piece of middleware mutates the raw headers (or a retry wrapper generates a new id) without calling the contextvar setter, the logging filter keeps the old value. This is a subtle async ordering problem unlike the earlier node init race.

tom: two-pronged fix idea: 1) canonicalize request-id updates to always call a helper e.g., redwood_telemetry.set_request_id(req, rid) that both updates req headers and the contextvar; 2) adjust the redaction sanitizer to never treat request-id as PII and ensure the logging filter reads the same source as otel span attrs (prefer a tiny shim: when setting span attribute also update contextvar). Add unit test that simulates `await` boundaries and concurrent tasks.

jonas-ci-bot: CI job started: telemetry-python-unit (will run tests including new concurrency test)

rekha: agreed. i'll implement set_request_id helper in the python SDK and change the middleware wrappers in sampleapp to call it instead of mutating headers directly. i'll also add an integration test that runs the concurrent_retries script in CI via tox matrix and fails if log request-id != span attribute for any request.

jasmin: workaround for now: set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info and use the env REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT_EXCEPTIONS=request-id,x-request-id in onboarding instructions. but we should avoid requiring that.

tom: also emit a telemetry metric telemetry.requestid.context_mismatch when our reconciler detects a difference between span attr and logging contextvar so we can surface frequency in hosted. Add a changelog entry: "Python SDK: ensure request-id set updates logging contextvar and span attribute atomically; add reconciliation metric."

rekha: I'll open PR w/ tests, CI changes, and a note in quickstarts. assigning to @tom for review.

jasmin: thanks team. this one was noisy in support because customers see spans with ids but logs with [REDACTED] or old ids and can't link them. Hoping the helper approach reduces cognitive load for sampleapp authors. :thumbsup:
